item.title: Conflicts, El Nino Worsening Hunger — UN Food Agencies
item.description: UN food agencies warned Friday of worsening hunger over the next six months in 16 mostly African areas, with ongoing conflicts exacerbating already dire conditions in countries like Sudan and Yemen. While armed conflict and violence are the main reasons for acute food insecurity around the globe, dramatic climate events, including El Nino, are another driver, the joint report from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP) said. The Rome-based agencies listed Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen as the areas of highest concern in its early warning about 16 “hunger hotspots” from December until May 2027. Famine remains a “plausible” risk in parts of Sudan — including North Darfur — and South Sudan, the report found. ‘Alarming levels of displacement’ The indoor cooking setup of a local food vendor, featuring large metal pots resting on industrial gas stoves. The stoves are connected directly to an orange gas cylinder running on the clean, smoke-free biogas produced by the biodigester. (Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV) The risk of worsening hunger comes amid a rise in “political violence events” around the world, up by more than 15 percent over the same period a year earlier, which has prompted “alarming levels of displacement in recent months”, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen. In the five countries most at risk, all repeatedly cited on the hotspot list since 2022, humanitarian assistance has declined by nearly two-thirds over the 2022-2025 period, from $5.1 billion to $2 billion. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” wrote FAO and WFP. While past humanitarian assistance helped avert famine, “the gains proved fragile and of limited duration: severe acute food insecurity risks — including risk of famine — re-emerged within a few years.” Also classified as a “very high concern” are Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo — which is also struggling to contend with an outbreak of Ebola — Palestine, and Haiti, where expanding gang violence has displaced 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access. New additions to the list are Chad, Uganda, the Southern Africa region and the Central American Dry Corridor, a tropical dry forest extending from Guatemala to Costa Rica, with the latter two regions expected to be hit by the effects of El Nino, adversely affecting crops. The list also includes Mali, Myanmar and Madagascar. “Targeted humanitarian action is urgently needed to save lives and livelihoods across all hunger hotspots,” read the report. “In hotspots of highest concern, such action is critical to prevent starvation and loss of life.” Too much or little rain El Nino — the ocean warming phenomenon that is disrupting weather patterns globally, provoking devastating droughts or in

item.title: 2027: Lokpobiri rallies Bayelsa West for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, has urged voters in Bayelsa West Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. Lokpobiri made the appeal on Thursday, November 26, during a pre-campaign sensitisation exercise organised by the Bayelsa West APC Campaign Directorate in Aleibiri, Ebedebiri and Agbere communities. Addressing party members, stakeholders and residents, the minister urged them to remain committed to the APC, saying sustained support for the party was necessary to consolidate the reforms and transformation being pursued by the Tinubu administration under its Renewed Hope Agenda. He said Tinubu had demonstrated the courage, vision and determination to reposition the country through what he described as bold reforms and purposeful leadership. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has remained committed to delivering on his Renewed Hope mandate and transforming our dear nation. The progress being made requires our collective support and commitment to ensure that the gains are sustained. We must therefore give him another mandate in 2027,” he said. The minister also called on the people to support all APC candidates, stressing that political unity, grassroots mobilisation and collective participation would be crucial to the party’s prospects in the elections. “I urge the good people of Bayelsa West to stand firmly with President Tinubu and all APC candidates. This is the time to consolidate our structures, strengthen our grassroots engagement and work together towards victory,” he added. The sensitisation exercise, according to the organisers, was part of the party’s efforts to strengthen grassroots mobilisation, encourage peaceful political participation and build support structures across Bayelsa West ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: Kwankwaso accuses Kano governor of plot to tarnish his image
item.description: Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has accused Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, of allegedly orchestrating a campaign to tarnish his reputation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso made the allegation in a statement issued on Friday, expressing concern over what he described as the alleged use of anti-corruption institutions, particularly the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), for political purposes. The former Kano State governor questioned the motives behind what he characterised as attempts to damage his public image, alleging that the anti-corruption agency was being drawn into political activities. He expressed concern that institutions established to fight corruption could be used to settle political scores, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. However, the allegations against Governor Yusuf remain claims by Kwankwaso and would require an independent response from the governor or his representatives. Adeleke was re-elected governor on August 15, 2026, defeating the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, by more than 60,000 votes. The inauguration, which was ongoing at the time of filing this report, attracted several political figures, including APC National Leader, Chief Bisi Akande; former Senate President, Bukola Saraki; and former APC National Secretary, Senator Iyiola Omisore. item.title: 2027: Emerging opposition coalition comprises displaced politicians — Lagos APC
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has criticised ongoing merger and coalition talks among opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections, describing the emerging alliance as an association of “internally displaced politicians” driven by personal grievances rather than a coherent vision for governance. The Lagos APC spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark on Friday, questioned the ideological consistency and sincerity of the political actors seeking to unite against President Bola Tinubu in 2027. According to Oladejo, the emerging alliance comprises former power brokers, ex-officeholders and frustrated aspirants who previously benefited from or helped shape the same political establishments they now criticise. He maintained that the coalition lacked a unified policy framework on critical national issues, including economic management, energy reforms, foreign exchange policy and national security. “What is being marketed to Nigerians as a formidable opposition coalition increasingly looks like an assembly of politically displaced persons, disgruntled power brokers, frustrated presidential aspirants and former beneficiaries of the very political establishments they now denounce,” the Lagos APC spokesman said. Reacting to another round of opposition consultations scheduled for Monday, Oladejo dismissed the repeated meetings as “political motion without movement”. He argued that bringing prominent political figures together under one roof did not automatically translate into grassroots electoral structures or administrative competence. Oladejo further contended that opposition rhetoric had become excessively focused on opposing Tinubu rather than presenting a credible alternative blueprint for governance. While acknowledging that the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had brought difficult adjustments for households and businesses, the Lagos APC maintained that the 2027 election would be determined by verifiable performance records, policy continuity and organisational strength rather than what it described as a “coalition of grievances”. item.title: 2027 Election:​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍‌‌​‍‍‌​ INEC procures 57,000 new BVAS devices
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission has procured 57,000 new BVAS for the 2027 general elections. Prof. Amupitan disclosed this on Thursday during a sensitisation seminar by the Diocese of Abuja, Anglican Communion, on Civil and Political Education with the theme “Why Your Vote Still Matters” Represented by the Deputy Director, Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Wilfred Ifogah, Prof. Amupitan said that the commission had also reduced the threshold from 1,250 to 850 voters per machine and cleaned the register through biometric audit. He said that with 51 days to the Jan. 16, 2027, presidential and National Assembly elections, civic responsibility must not be outsourced. Amupitan said INEC would on Saturday conduct a nationwide mock accreditation exercise in two polling units per ward to test upgrades ahead of 2027. According to him, over 10.77 million new registrants were recorded during the Continuous Voter Registration, while over 1.6 million invalid records were removed, bringing the verified register to over 100 million voters, including 232,658 persons with disabilities. He said INEC had also upgraded its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, with automated checks for over-voting and arithmetic consistency on Form EC8A before transmission. The INEC boss urged citizens to resist vote buying, divisive politics and inflammatory language, noting that Sections 95, 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026 prescribe stiff penalties for electoral violence and hate speech. Also speaking, a legal practitioner, Mr Emeka Etiaba, SAN, said over-judicialisation of elections was eroding public confidence. Etiaba said trust is earned, not commanded, stressing that INEC and the judiciary must deliver credible processes in 2027 to restore confidence. He noted that technicalities, poor petition drafting and non-justiciable innovations often deny determination of cases on merit, leaving a few judges to decide outcomes involving thousands of voters. He said innovations such as AI validation on IReV, though laudable administratively, must be backed by law to be enforceable in court. Speaking at the event, the Primate of the Church of Nigeria, Anglican Communion, Most Rev. Henry Ndukuba, urged Nigerians, especially youths, to actively participate in the 2027 general elections. According to him, their votes remain critical to deepening democracy and national development. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the seminar is part of activities marking the 37th anniversary of the diocese and Carnival for Christ 2026. Ndukuba said the church organised the seminar to sensitise citizens on their civic responsibility ahead of the polls, and the 2027 electioneering campaigns were already underway, with general elections scheduled for January 2027. item.title: Questions about Tinubu’s identity come up anytime he’s about to win election — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed renewed questions about President Bola Tinubu’s background and identity, saying the controversies resurface whenever the president is on the verge of winning an election. Fashola described the questions as needless distractions, insisting that Tinubu had met the constitutional requirements to contest the presidency and that Nigerians had already settled the matter through their votes. He said the controversy had persisted for more than two decades but had not stopped Tinubu from winning elections, expressing confidence that the president would secure another victory in 2027. Fashola spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to questions about the perceived secrecy surrounding Tinubu’s background and identity. “I think that these matters have carried on for all of 20-something years. So, every time he’s at the threshold of winning an election, these issues come, and you know what always happens: he wins,” he said. “So history is about to repeat itself again. He’s going to win. These are needless distractions. They don’t answer a fundamental question. And I’ve said about minimum qualification. He has met it,” the former governor added. Fashola questioned the relevance of the controversies to Nigerians, saying opposition politicians should focus on issues that would improve the lives of citizens rather than repeatedly raising questions about Tinubu’s background. “The question I will focus upon if I were those fragmented opposition is how does this help the people whose mandate I want? It doesn’t help them,” he said. The former minister of works also argued that some of the issues had previously been subjected to legal proceedings and investigations, including during the 1999 political period and the last presidential election. Drawing on his experience as a legal practitioner, Fashola said there was a need to allow an end to prolonged disputes, invoking the legal principle that litigation must eventually come to a conclusion. “I believe parts of this were litigated in the last election. They were litigated in 1999. It was the subject of a House investigation in that period. You keep referring to my other life as a legal practitioner, there’s a principle in that life. There’s something we say, a principle that there must be an end to litigation. It’s enough,” he said. Fashola said Nigerians had moved on from the controversy, citing Tinubu’s victory in the 2023 presidential election as evidence, and predicted that voters would reaffirm their position in 2027. “They pursue it at their own choice, but I think the Nigerian people have left that subject behind. They have left it behind with their votes in 2023. They will reaffirm it in 2027,” he said. item.title: Mock Accreditation: Sanwo-Olu Cancels November Environmental Sanitation Exercise
item.description: Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has cancelled the November edition of the state’s monthly environmental sanitation exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026. The development was disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Kunle Adeshina. The decision was taken to allow the smooth conduct of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise scheduled for the same day. In an updated statement issued on Friday and signed by the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Gaji Tajudeen, the governor said the INEC exercise would hold between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. This file photo shows an ad hoc official of INEC accrediting a voter with a BVAS machine. The mock exercise is expected to cover two polling units in each of Nigeria’s 8,838 Registration Areas. According to the statement, the governor considered it necessary to cancel the sanitation exercise to prevent any disruption to the commencement of the mock accreditation, which is also scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. The state government, however, urged residents to keep their surroundings clean regularly rather than wait for the monthly sanitation exercise. item.title: People who opposed Tinubu now work with him — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain former allies and reconcile political opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity and build consensus. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question for those who want to vote,” Fashola said. He asked why many of those who worked with Tinubu during his time as Lagos governor had remained with him, while political associates of other candidates had moved on. “Where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so out of office when he wasn’t a president. That’s a very good answer to the question,” he said. Fashola said the loyalty of Tinubu’s associates reflected his ability to work with others and manage disagreements without abandoning relationships, adding that such qualities were important for a president leading a country with diverse interests. “It shows an ability to work with others. If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team, and you don’t just get up and jump away when there is crisis in the fold,” he said. He contrasted Tinubu’s political experience with that of other candidates, saying the president remained in the APC despite internal crises, while others left the parties through which they rose to prominence. “There was crisis in the APC. He didn’t leave the party. The others have left the parties that brought them to prominence,” Fashola said. The former governor further argued that Tinubu had expanded his political alliances by bringing former opponents into his fold, including those who once strongly opposed him. “All the people who opposed Tinubu when he used to be called the last man standing. All of them are now working with him. Not just those who worked with him before; those who oppose him are now working with him,” he said. item.title: From fuel subsidy return to Ajaokuta revival; Atiku’s 2027 promises so far
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, tackle insecurity, create jobs and revive key infrastructure projects if elected president in 2027. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate has made the pledges at campaign rallies in Sokoto, Bauchi, Yobe and Kogi states, while presenting his proposed policies as measures to reduce the cost of living and improve economic conditions. At the ADC presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on November 4 , Atiku promised to restore petrol subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders to encourage trade and tackle insecurity, including kidnapping, banditry and terrorism. He also pledged to reduce the cost of pilgrimage for Muslim and Christian faithful. Atiku said restoring petrol subsidy would help reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices of essential goods. He also argued that reopening the land borders would benefit farmers, traders and transport operators by stimulating cross-border commerce. At a rally in Bauchi State on November 14, Atiku extended his subsidy promise to electricity, saying he would restore both petroleum and electricity subsidies if elected. He also pledged to strengthen security, particularly in the North-East, resume oil exploration in the Kolmani field and continue the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project. “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue,” he said at the Bauchi rally. At a campaign rally in Yobe State on November 15, Atiku again promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, while pledging to address insecurity and create employment opportunities for young Nigerians. “Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy,” he said, adding that he would also restore electricity subsidy. He further promised that his administration would work to ensure peace returned to Yobe and other parts of the country, and that young Nigerians would have access to employment opportunities. In Kogi State on November 24 , Atiku campaigned on an “Affordable Life” message, promising to reduce fuel costs, support local production and improve Nigerians’ purchasing power. He said his proposals were aimed at easing the pressure on households, workers and small businesses. At the rally in Lokoja, he also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill through foreign investment, without relying on government funding for the project. He promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger to enable the port to serve other states and create employment opportunities. “I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. item.title: Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Singer-songwriter and record producer Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has said the “rig and die” slogan sounds correct as a response to election rigging, but warned that innocent people must not be caught up in the resulting violence. He spoke in an interview on Nigeria Info’s WhatsUpLagos show while responding to the slogan ahead of the 2027 elections. The ace singer said frustration over impunity had made calls for severe punishment understandable, while stressing that allegations of rigging must be proven. “You know when a situation gets to a certain point, like right now we’re like on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make you make some kind of statements. This statement sounds correct. It should be like that, actually.” He said the slogan reflected a demand for stronger consequences for election rigging. “If you rig, the punishments should be very severe to deter people from rigging.” 2Baba added: “So the statement itself is rig or die. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzle money and die. Na death penalty for China for embezzlement.” He said Nigeria needed serious deterrence for crimes, including kidnapping, and that people were frustrated by what he described as a lack of consequences. “We’re in a stage where we need, we need serious deterrence, anybody who kidnaps is supposed to face serious consequences. “Because it’s getting too much, and people are just getting away with everything. You understand what I’m saying? So for me, the statement itself, it shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone by. So for me, I don’t see nothing wrong with that statement.” However, he warned against innocent people being harmed in the name of enforcing the slogan. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this fight because some people might not rig, they might just be there. It could be jungle justice without proving that the person actually rigged.” He said the burden of proof should rest on the accusers, while reiterating his support for the statement. “So that’s where, that’s where it becomes dangerous. So the burden of proof should be on the accused person, but the statement in itself, I am in full support of it.” The post Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nvidia: Women Raise Concerns Over Jensen Huang’s Return
item.description: News of Jensen Huang’s shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. The image was based on a real photo taken in 2024 when Trump survived an assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied that Huang, too, had survived a bid to take him out. For many women, though, the image spoke insultingly to longstanding frustrations about sexism, double standards and a lack of accountability for men in power — across politics and business. Meanwhile, many “tech bros” rushed to Huang’s defense over the past couple of weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk was among many people who signed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP Venture capitalist Jason Calacanis described Huang as a “hero” and downplayed the scandal that led to Huang’s resignation as less important than the United States winning the AI race against China. “They’re standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want,” Cleo Capital Managing Director Sarah Kunst told AFP. Part of the problem might be “hero worship,” she said. It also reflects the tech industry’s mythology around “founder mode” — the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives. Huang resigned on November 12 from Nvidia, the company he cofounded and has led for more than three decades, amid allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman that US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, triggering national security concerns. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Another of Huanga’s alleged lovers was a subordinate at Nvidia. “This is a great example of why integrity matters,” Kunst said. “As soon as I heard about the honeypot element, it was clear to me that there were lapses in judgment that were really big.” On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Then President Donald Trump intervened. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC, referring to Huang’s reinstatement. Trump himself was found liable in 2023 for sexual assault and defamation and ordered to pay millions as punishment. item.title: I belong to APC but will protect all parties — Defence Minister
item.description: The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, has said his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) does not prevent him from carrying out his responsibility to provide security for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. Musa, a retired general, said he was entitled to associate with the ruling party because he was no longer serving in the military. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Arise Television, where he was asked to explain his participation in APC political activities and how he intended to separate his party affiliation from his official duties. “Well, I’m not a military man. I belong to APC, I’m allowed to do that,” he said. The former Chief of Defence Staff maintained that his appearances at political events were also an opportunity to assess security arrangements and ensure that security agencies were performing their duties. He stressed, however, that the responsibility applied to all political parties. “I always want to make sure that whatever is happening anywhere, I go there to ensure that the security forces are doing what they should, and we can do that for everybody. It’s not just for APC. “We are free-minded, we are fair-minded to everybody. We want Nigeria to be safe. We’ll never be a party to any violence,” he said. The minister said President Bola Tinubu had repeatedly cautioned members of his administration against electoral violence. “I know the President has told us on several occasions when we meet, ‘I do not want a violent election. It is not worth it,’” he added. Musa also pledged that the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces would collaborate with political parties and other stakeholders to ensure credible elections in 2027. “Nigerians must understand that we must make our elections free and fair and credible. So we, members of the Armed Forces and the Defence, will ensure that we work together with everyone to make the elections free. “We want every Nigerian to be free to come out and vote for whoever he wants,” he said. On complaints by opposition parties about political violence, Musa argued that disagreements within political parties could also trigger clashes. “Within all the parties, yes! We have found sometimes you see them because somebody feels somebody shouldn’t be there or his name was replaced for whatever reason, then he wants to sabotage from within. So the enemy is not only outside, it’s also within. “Whether the opposition or the party in government, violence is a no-no. And Defence is standing on its feet to ensure that the coming election is free and fair. Whatever it takes for us to do that, we will do that,” he said. item.title: Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world. “I think he’s absolutely fine,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Huang, Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.” Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export controls. His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making. “I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Trump said Thursday. “So I really… think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world,” Trump said of the effort to back Huang. Asked if he had spoken with Huang since his reinstatement was announced, Trump said no, but then later said: “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.” He also praised Huang’s wife as “phenomenal.” The post Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027 Elections: INEC raises alarm, warns violence may hurt polls
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. This came as the Federal Government assured voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties of protection before, during and after the elections. Speaking at a Strategic Election Security Conference jointly convened by INEC and the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, Amupitan said Nigeria had witnessed a disturbing escalation in political intolerance, inflammatory rhetoric and coordinated attacks since the commencement of campaigns in August 2026. Addressing political parties, he said: “Signing peace accords in Abuja while tolerating or financing thuggery in the states is a contradiction our democracy can no longer afford.” He warned that INEC would not succumb to threats or intimidation. “We will neither be intimidated nor blackmailed into compromising our neutrality, and every attack on INEC personnel, facilities, or materials will be met with the full weight of the law,” INEC chairman said. Amupitan said responsibility for electoral violence extended beyond those directly involved in attacks, stressing that political party leaders must be held accountable for the conduct of their candidates and supporters. He said: “Accountability does not end with the foot soldiers who throw stones or wield weapons,” adding that “party leadership bears moral and political responsibility for the conduct of its candidates, campaign councils, and youth wings”. item.title: 2027: 2Baba backs ‘rig and die’ slogan, demands severe penalties
item.description: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has backed the controversial “rig and die” slogan associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying anyone caught manipulating election results in 2027 should face severe punishment. The singer, however, cautioned against innocent people being victimised in the process, insisting that elections should not be treated as warfare. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Nigeria Info 99.3, where he described Nigeria’s political atmosphere as tense and said the slogan reflected growing public frustration over the country’s situation. “You know, when the situation gets to a certain point, like right now, we’re on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make people make some kinds of statements. “The statement sounds correct, right? It sounds correct. It should be like that, actually. For the circumstances. Like, if you rig, the punishments will be very severe to deter people from rigging,” 2Baba said. The singer said he saw nothing wrong with the slogan, arguing that stringent penalties would discourage electoral malpractice. “The statement itself is ‘rig and die’. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzlement and die. Now, there’s that penalty for embezzlement in China,” he said. 2Baba also called for severe consequences for kidnappers, particularly those targeting schools, arguing that the absence of adequate deterrence had allowed criminal activities to persist. “We’re in a state where we need serious deterrence for anybody who kidnaps in our schools to face serious consequences, so that others will not do it. Because it’s getting too much and people are just getting away with everything,” he said. The ‘African Queen’ crooner said the slogan reflected the level of frustration among Nigerians but warned against punishing people without evidence of wrongdoing. “For me, the statement itself shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone bad. So, for me, I don’t see anything wrong with that statement. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this,” he added. During the interview, the presenter recalled 2Baba’s longstanding advocacy for peaceful electoral participation, including his message urging Nigerians to vote rather than fight during elections. Asked about Nigerians who might sell their votes because of economic hardship, the singer described the situation as unfortunate, noting that people facing difficult conditions could easily become vulnerable to manipulation. He also called for proper reorientation, urging Nigerians to address internal challenges rather than allow external interests to influence the country. The “rig and die” slogan has featured prominently in political discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly among supporters of the NDC and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi.
